correctness.rationale: Each nonempty color class is precisely a vertex odd-independent set. With unmatched vertices on both sides, a single-side class touching any matched endpoint must be singleton; a cross-side class must be exactly one deleted matched pair; all other classes are odd blocks of unmatched vertices. The converse is verified class-by-class. Labeled partition enumeration and the odd-block exponential formula give the polynomial, and equality conditions give the minimum and number of optimizers. Exhaustive independent graph-based tests matched 30 full profiles; these finite checks are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The all-color enumerator and complete minimum-coloring classification for non-spanning matching deletions have no covering implication in the read primary references or closest public scientific results. The spanning odd-crown theorem gives an optimum only at a disjoint boundary; complete multipartite odd independence covers the undeleted boundary; general bounds and odd-independent-set inequalities do not determine partition profiles. Targeted literature and mathematical record searches found no dominating claim; unindexed equivalent work remains possible.
residual_risks: The literature search is not exhaustive: a differently termed full enumeration could exist outside the indexed sources.
The full-matching saturation boundary is omitted; direct transfer of the formula across that boundary is generally invalid.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact, motivated, all-color enumerator for strong odd colorings of the natural three-parameter family \(K_{a,b}-M_t\), together with a complete extremizer census. Its structural decomposition into paired endpoints and odd partitions of two unmatched sides reveals an edge-deletion sensitivity of opposite sign depending on part parity. This is not a mere relabeling of complete bipartite or odd crown results; both known endpoint structures fail to cover the interior family.
